data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's evidence criterion requires showing the panel's accuracy is insensitive to checklist corruption but sensitive to aggregation method within a single evaluation. A single evaluation cannot show insensitivity to corruption unless it includes a corrupted-checklist arm, but then the panel is no longer following the explicit checklist specified by the problem — it is a different intervention. The target thus cannot distinguish genuine checklist-mediated gain from aggregation gain using the evaluation it describes, because detecting insensitivity to corruption requires comparing across checklist conditions, which a single evaluation of the stated intervention does not provide. The countercondition conceding that errors may be correlated (e.g., all follow the same wrong rule) further undermines the independence assumption on which the entire wisdom-of-crowds mechanism depends.
